notes: §1985:VII.2.7.4 GR1: "The PADDING CHARACTER clause specifies the character which is to be used for block padding on sequential files."; padding beyond the last logical record of a block is bypassed on input and written on output, and "a logical record which consists solely of padding characters will be ignored". The clause is hardware dependent (§1985:p.XVII-94 item 5: "dependent upon whether padding characters are applicable to the device type to which the file is assigned"), and GR2 of the same clause gives the result where they are not: no creation, no recognition. That is the only arm this implementation has. Every assignable device is a host file, SequentialConnector.Write stores one logical record per physical record and Read returns each stored record, so no physical record has an unused position for a padding character to fill (§1985:III.2, Padding Character: "An alphanumeric character used to fill the unused character positions in a physical record."). paddingCharacterClause parses the clause on the file control entry and nothing is kept; VisitPaddingCharacterClause is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, obsolete COBOL0903 at 2002, COBOL0902 from 2014). Probed at 85: under BLOCK CONTAINS 4 RECORDS and PADDING CHARACTER IS "*", three 5-character records make a 15-byte file with no fill, and all three are read back, a record of five asterisks included. The absence of block padding is stated in docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.20 (§1985:I.1.5.2.5.1 asks that it be specified); docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no 1985 line for it. The clause's operand rules are not asked (kb/Work PB5070, the SR rows), and the clause is accepted on a relative or indexed entry, where 1985 does not print it (the finding recorded on 1985-FMT-IX.2.3.2). The witness writes three records, one holding asterisks, under BLOCK CONTAINS 4 RECORDS and reads them back.

next.reason: 1985: "The PADDING CHARACTER clause specifies the character which is to be used for block padding on sequential files."; 2023: "No PADDING CHARACTER clause among the 2023 file-control clauses; BLOCK CONTAINS only mentions padding as area outside a record". No 2023 clause holds the PADDING CHARACTER feature. No candidate defines a padding character or bypassing/filling padding on input/output, so the clause is dropped.
